title.en: Volume 285 Biographies 72: Wang Zishou, Yuan Zhouzuo, Li Shihong, Duo Hong An, Wang Xu, Zhang Mengqiu
title.raw: 卷285 列傳七十二 王紫绶 袁州佐 黎士宏 多宏安 王𦈡 张孟球

sentences.zh: 列傳七十二

translations.literal: Biographies 72
translations.idiomatic: Biography 72

sentences.zh: 王紫綬袁州佐黎士弘多弘安佟國聘王繻田呈瑞張孟球

translations.literal: Wang Zishou, Yuan Zhouzuo, Li Shihong, Duo Hong'an, Tong Guopin, Wang Xu, Tian Chengrui, Zhang Mengqiu
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zishou, Yuan Zhouzuo, Li Shihong, Duo Hong'an, Tong Guopin, Wang Xu, Tian Chengrui, and Zhang Mengqiu

sentences.zh: 王紫綬，字金章，河南祥符人。

translations.literal: Wang Zishou, courtesy name Jinzhang, was a man of Xiangfu in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zishou, whose courtesy name was Jinzhang, came from Xiangfu in Henan.

sentences.zh: 順治三年進士，選庶吉士。

translations.literal: In the third year of Shunzhi he became a jinshi and was selected as a bachelor of the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the third year of Shunzhi and was chosen as a Hanlin bachelor.

sentences.zh: 散館，授編修。

translations.literal: Upon leaving the academy, he was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: When his term at the academy ended, he received an appointment as compiler.

sentences.zh: 乞養歸，僑寓蘇門山中，從孫奇逢講學。

translations.literal: He requested leave to care for his parents and returned home, living as a sojourner in the Sumen Mountains and studying under Sun Qifeng.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to retire and support his parents, settled in the Sumen Mountains, and pursued his studies with Sun Qifeng.

sentences.zh: 居十有七年，母歿，服闋，康熙十二年，授江西贛南道副使。

translations.literal: He dwelt there for seventeen years; when his mother died and his mourning ended, in the twelfth year of Kangxi he was appointed Vice Commissioner of the Gannan Circuit in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He remained there seventeen years. After his mother's death and the close of mourning, in the twelfth year of Kangxi he was made Vice Commissioner of the Gannan Circuit in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 吳三桂反，贛南總兵劉進寶有謀略，紫綬推誠結納，預籌防禦。

translations.literal: When Wu Sangui rebelled, the Gannan regional commander Liu Jinbao was skilled in strategy; Zishou won him over with sincerity and made advance plans for defense.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Sangui rose in rebellion, the Gannan regional commander Liu Jinbao proved a capable strategist. Zishou won his trust and laid defensive plans well ahead of time.

sentences.zh: 既而江西降眾屯墾者相繼叛，惟贛南尚未動。

translations.literal: Before long the surrendered masses who had been settled to farm in Jiangxi rebelled one after another, but Gannan alone had not yet stirred.
translations.idiomatic: Soon surrendered settlers farming in Jiangxi were rebelling in succession, yet Gannan alone still held firm.

sentences.zh: 紫綬與進寶謀：「閩、粵反已見端，贛南扼其間，應援前朝故事，設巡撫以資鎮攝。

translations.literal: Zishou plotted with Jinbao: "The rebellions in Fujian and Guangdong have already shown their beginnings; Gannan stands between them and should follow the precedent of earlier dynasties by establishing a governor-general to strengthen control."
translations.idiomatic: Zishou and Jinbao agreed: "Rebellion in Fujian and Guangdong is already taking shape. Gannan lies between them; we should follow earlier precedent and establish a governor-general to hold the region in check."

sentences.zh: 」申疆吏上請，允之。

translations.literal: " They reported this through the frontier officials to the throne, and it was approved.
translations.idiomatic: They submitted the proposal through the provincial authorities, and the court approved it.

sentences.zh: 十四年，賊勢益熾，山寇蜂起，鎮兵疲於奔命，乃練鄉勇以輔之，屢殺賊有功。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year the rebels grew fiercer, mountain bandits swarmed forth, and the garrison troops were worn out running to and fro; he therefore trained local militia to assist them and repeatedly killed rebels with merit.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year rebel strength mounted and mountain bandits rose everywhere. The garrison was exhausted chasing them, so he trained local militia to reinforce the army and won repeated victories against the rebels.

sentences.zh: 十五年，巡撫白色純及進寶先後卒官，參將周球領鎮兵。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year the governor-general Bai Sechun and Jinbao died in office one after another, and the deputy commander Zhou Qiu took command of the garrison troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year Governor-General Bai Sechun and Jinbao died in succession on duty, and Deputy Commander Zhou Qiu assumed command of the garrison.

sentences.zh: 三桂將高得捷、韓大任據吉安，餉道絕，屬縣相繼陷。

translations.literal: Sangui's generals Gao Dejie and Han Daren held Ji'an; the supply route was cut off, and subordinate counties fell one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Sangui's generals Gao Dejie and Han Daren seized Ji'an, severing the supply lines, and the surrounding counties fell in turn.

sentences.zh: 大任屢致書勸降，送偽署巡撫劄，紫綬斬其使。

translations.literal: Daren repeatedly sent letters urging surrender and delivered a forged commission as governor-general; Zishou executed his envoy.
translations.idiomatic: Daren wrote again and again urging him to surrender and sent a forged appointment as governor-general. Zishou had the messenger beheaded.

sentences.zh: 球以乏餉為難，紫綬集士商勸輸間架稅，得白金四萬畀球，餉以無缺。

translations.literal: Qiu found the lack of provisions a difficulty; Zishou gathered gentry and merchants to urge payment of a house-tax surcharge, obtained forty thousand taels of silver and gave them to Qiu, and supplies were never wanting.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu was hamstrung by the shortage of rations. Zishou rallied local gentry and merchants to levy a building-tax surcharge, raised forty thousand taels of silver for Qiu, and kept the army supplied without interruption.

sentences.zh: 鎮南將軍覺羅舒恕率禁旅下廣東，為尚之信將嚴自明所敗，兵退，距贛州三十里。

translations.literal: The Pacifier of the South, Aisin Gioro Shushu, led the banner troops south into Guangdong and was defeated by Shang Zhixin's general Yan Ziming; the army retreated to within thirty li of Ganzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Pacifier of the South, Aisin Gioro Shushu, marched into Guangdong at the head of the banner army but was routed by Shang Zhixin's general Yan Ziming. His force fell back to within thirty li of Ganzhou.

sentences.zh: 自明約得捷由吉安會師夾擊。

translations.literal: Ziming agreed with Dejie to join forces from Ji'an and strike from both sides.
translations.idiomatic: Ziming arranged with Dejie to unite their armies at Ji'an and attack Ganzhou from two sides.

sentences.zh: 紫綬薦降將許盛率所部漳州水兵五百人益師，夜泅江斫賊營，禁旅繼之，擊敗自明。

translations.literal: Zishou recommended the surrendered general Xu Sheng, who led five hundred Zhangzhou marines under his command to reinforce the army; by night they swam the river and stormed the rebel camp, the banner troops followed, and Ziming was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Zishou put forward the surrendered general Xu Sheng and his five hundred Zhangzhou marines. They swam the river at night and raided the rebel camp; the banner troops pressed the attack, and Ziming was driven off.

sentences.zh: 得捷等勢孤，不敢复窺贛。

translations.literal: Dejie and the others, isolated in strength, did not dare again to cast their eyes toward Gan.
translations.idiomatic: Cut off and weakened, Dejie and his allies no longer dared threaten Ganzhou.

sentences.zh: 鎮兵出剿土寇，掠村民，紫綬曰：「鄉民脅從，若並以賊論，贛南二府十六縣將無孑遺。

translations.literal: The garrison troops went out to suppress local bandits and plundered villagers; Zishou said: "The rural people were coerced into following them; if all are treated as rebels, the two prefectures and sixteen counties of Gannan will leave not a soul alive."
translations.idiomatic: When the garrison marched out against local bandits they looted the countryside. Zishou warned: "These villagers followed under duress. Treat them all as rebels and the two prefectures and sixteen counties of Gannan will be wiped clean."

sentences.zh: 」戒鎮將毋妄發兵，飭有司招撫，分別留遣，賑濟難民，境內稍安。

translations.literal: " He admonished the regional commander not to send troops rashly, ordered the local officials to offer amnesty and pacification, distinguished those to be kept or sent away, and relieved the suffering of refugees, and within the borders there was gradual peace.
translations.idiomatic: He forbade the commander to deploy troops recklessly, ordered civil officials to offer amnesty, sorted who should stay or leave, and fed the destitute until the region grew calm again.

sentences.zh: 乃規复萬安、泰和兩縣。

translations.literal: He then planned to recover the two counties of Wan'an and Taihe.
translations.idiomatic: He then set out to recover Wan'an and Taihe.

sentences.zh: 自螺山間道達墨潭，可登舟，於是南昌道始通，運餉銀十萬至。

translations.literal: By a mountain path from Luoshan he reached Motan, where boats could be boarded; thus the route to Nanchang was opened for the first time, and one hundred thousand taels of silver in supplies arrived.
translations.idiomatic: He opened a trail from Luoshan to Motan where boats could be taken, restoring the route to Nanchang for the first time in years and bringing in a hundred thousand taels of silver in supplies.

sentences.zh: 又發附近倉穀贍軍，人心大定。

translations.literal: He also issued grain from nearby granaries to feed the army, and popular sentiment was greatly settled.
translations.idiomatic: He released grain from nearby storehouses to feed the troops, and morale steadied across the region.

sentences.zh: 巡撫佟國禎亦自間道至，始知紫綬已擢浙江督糧道參政。

translations.literal: The governor-general Tong Guozhen also arrived by a secret route and only then learned that Zishou had already been promoted to Administrative Commissioner of the Zhejiang Grain Transport Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Tong Guozhen reached him by the same back trail and learned only then that Zishou had already been promoted to Administrative Commissioner on the Zhejiang grain-transport circuit.

sentences.zh: 贛南久不通驛報，大學士李霨言於朝曰：「紫綬死守危疆，三年於茲。

translations.literal: Gannan had long been without courier reports; Grand Secretary Li Ji said at court: "Zishou has held this perilous frontier to the death for three years now."
translations.idiomatic: Gannan had been cut off from courier reports for so long that Grand Secretary Li Ji told the court: "Zishou has held this desperate frontier for three years running."

sentences.zh: 為國惜才，援而出之，猶可大用。

translations.literal: For the state's sake cherish his talent; draw him out by promotion, and he may still be put to great use.
translations.idiomatic: The state should not waste such a man; pull him out while there is still time and he can serve on a larger scale.

sentences.zh: 」故有是擢。

translations.literal: " Therefore this promotion came about.
translations.idiomatic: That was how he came to receive the promotion.

sentences.zh: 紫綬聞命泣下。

translations.literal: When Zishou heard the order he wept.
translations.idiomatic: Zishou wept when he received the appointment.

sentences.zh: 十六年，上官，察積弊，歎曰：「糧官不可為也！

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he reported to his superiors, examined long-standing abuses, and sighed: "The post of grain official cannot be held!"
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he took up his new post, surveyed entrenched abuses, and exclaimed: "This grain office is impossible!"

sentences.zh: 漕截減而軍困，白折浮而民困，吾安忍竭東南之澤而漁之？

translations.literal: Grain transport deductions leave the army in distress, inflated silver conversions leave the people in distress—how can I bear to drain the bounty of the southeast and fish it dry?
translations.idiomatic: Cuts to the grain transport starve the army; inflated silver conversions crush the people. How could I drain the wealth of the southeast to fill official coffers?

sentences.zh: 」一月即引疾去。

translations.literal: " After one month he cited illness and resigned.
translations.idiomatic: Within a month he pleaded illness and resigned.

sentences.zh: 迨開博學鴻詞科，魏象樞以紫綬與湯斌同薦入試。

translations.literal: When the special examination for erudition and literary excellence was opened, Wei Xiangshu recommended Zishou together with Tang Bin to enter the examination.
translations.idiomatic: When the special erudition examination was convened, Wei Xiangshu nominated Zishou along with Tang Bin to sit for it.

sentences.zh: 放還。

translations.literal: He was sent home.
translations.idiomatic: He was dismissed and sent home.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 袁州佐，字左之，山東濟寧人。

translations.literal: Yuan Zhouzuo, courtesy name Zuozhi, was a man of Jining in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zhouzuo, whose courtesy name was Zuozhi, came from Jining in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 順治十二年進士，授陝西乾州知州。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Shunzhi he became a jinshi and was appointed magistrate of Qianzhou in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the twelfth year of Shunzhi and was appointed magistrate of Qianzhou in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 入為工部員外郎，遷郎中。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as a vice director in the Ministry of Works and was promoted to director.
translations.idiomatic: He was called to the capital as a vice director in the Ministry of Works and later promoted to director.

sentences.zh: 有清直聲，胥吏不敢牟利。

translations.literal: He had a reputation for integrity and uprightness, and clerks did not dare to seek profit.
translations.idiomatic: His reputation for integrity was such that clerks dared not profit at public expense.

sentences.zh: 時山陵工巨，經費浩穰，州佐曰：「民困極矣，寸縑尺縷，皆閭閻膏血！

translations.literal: At that time the imperial tomb works were vast and expenditures enormous; Zhouzuo said: "The people are in extreme distress—every inch of silk and every foot of thread is the lifeblood of the common households!"
translations.idiomatic: Imperial tomb construction was then at its height and costs were staggering. Zhouzuo protested: "The people are at their limit. Every scrap of cloth comes from their blood and sweat."

sentences.zh: 」力清乾沒，司焚帛，省金錢鉅萬。

translations.literal: " He vigorously cleared embezzlement; the office for burning sacrificial silk saved tens of thousands in cash.
translations.idiomatic: He rooted out embezzlement and, by reforming the office that burned sacrificial silk, saved tens of thousands in silver.

sentences.zh: 出為陝西甘山道僉事。

translations.literal: He went out as an assistant commissioner of the Ganshan Circuit in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted abroad as assistant commissioner of the Ganshan Circuit in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 青海蒙古諸部覬得大草灘為牧地。

translations.literal: The Mongol tribes of Qinghai coveted obtaining Dacaotan as pastureland.
translations.idiomatic: The Mongol tribes of Qinghai were pressing to take Dacaotan as grazing land.

sentences.zh: 康熙九年，偕提督張勇度地畫界，堅拒，寢其議。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Kangxi, together with Regional Commander Zhang Yong he surveyed the land and drew the boundary, firmly refusing them, and the proposal was shelved.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Kangxi he joined Regional Commander Zhang Yong in surveying the border and held the line firm, and the proposal was dropped.

sentences.zh: 自後青海蒙古諸部人不敢复窺邊。

translations.literal: From then on the people of the Mongol tribes of Qinghai did not dare again to cast their eyes toward the border.
translations.idiomatic: After that the Qinghai Mongols no longer dared probe the frontier.

sentences.zh: 歲協西寧餽運，負載千里，甘州民苦之，州佐力請得罷。

translations.literal: Each year they assisted Xining's transport of supplies, carrying loads a thousand li; the people of Ganzhou suffered from this, and Zhouzuo pressed strongly until it was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Every year Ganzhou had to haul supplies a thousand li to support Xining, and the people were crushed by the burden. Zhouzuo petitioned until the practice was abolished.

sentences.zh: 甘州駐兵數千，待餉急，力為籌備，軍得宿飽。

translations.literal: Several thousand troops were stationed at Ganzhou and urgently awaited rations; he strove to prepare supplies, and the army was always well fed.
translations.idiomatic: Several thousand troops were stationed at Ganzhou and needed rations urgently. He threw himself into provisioning them, and the army never went hungry.

sentences.zh: 十年，遷直隸口北道參議。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was transferred to Administrative Supervisor of the Koubei Circuit in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was transferred to Administrative Supervisor of the Koubei Circuit in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 地確民貧，逋課積累，倉儲歷歲侵漁，耗蝕無算。

translations.literal: The land was barren and the people poor; tax arrears piled up, and granaries year after year were preyed upon, with incalculable waste.
translations.idiomatic: The soil was poor and the people impoverished. Tax arrears mounted, and year after year granary officials plundered the stores until the losses were beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 州佐請按籍覈實，清宿蠹。

translations.literal: Zhouzuo requested verification against the registers to clear long-standing corruption.
translations.idiomatic: Zhouzuo asked to audit the registers and root out entrenched corruption.

sentences.zh: 大吏懼以失察得罪，陽韙而陰沮之。

translations.literal: The high officials feared being punished for failure of oversight; they praised him openly while obstructing him in secret.
translations.idiomatic: Senior officials feared being charged with negligence; they praised him to his face while undermining him behind the scenes.

sentences.zh: 州佐擘畫盤錯，致疾乞休，未去官，卒。

translations.literal: Zhouzuo took up the tangled tasks and fell ill requesting retirement; before he had left office, he died.
translations.idiomatic: Zhouzuo threw himself into the knotted problems until illness forced him to request retirement. He died before he could leave office.

sentences.zh: 州佐在甘州久，言邊境要害戰守狀，原委斠然。

translations.literal: Zhouzuo had long been at Ganzhou and spoke of the border's strategic points and conditions of war and defense with every detail clear.
translations.idiomatic: After long service at Ganzhou, Zhouzuo could explain every strategic point on the frontier and how to defend it with complete clarity.

sentences.zh: 謂邊地民稀，宜用開中法，分河東鹽引三之一輸粟河西資軍食；

translations.literal: He said that in the borderlands the population was sparse and the kaizhong method should be used, allotting one-third of the Hedong salt certificates to deliver grain to Hexi to supply the army's food;
translations.idiomatic: He argued that the frontier was sparsely settled and should use the kaizhong system, dedicating one-third of Hedong salt certificates to shipping grain west of the river for the army's rations;

sentences.zh: 又宜簡練鄉勇，拔置卒伍，不待召募，可坐收精銳。

translations.literal: and that local militia should be selected and trained, drawn into the ranks of soldiers—without waiting for recruitment, elite troops could be gathered at ease.
translations.idiomatic: and that local militia should be drilled and drafted into the ranks so that crack troops could be raised without waiting on recruitment.

sentences.zh: 時詔簡監司具才望者入為卿貳，州佐在選，會卒，未及用。

translations.literal: At that time an edict selected circuit intendants of talent and reputation to enter the capital as vice ministers; Zhouzuo was among those chosen, but he happened to die and was never employed.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then called circuit officials of talent to the capital for vice-ministerial posts. Zhouzuo was on the list, but he died before he could be appointed.

sentences.zh: 黎士弘，字媿曾，福建長汀人。

translations.literal: Li Shihong, courtesy name Kuizeng, was a man of Changting in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shihong, whose courtesy name was Kuizeng, came from Changting in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 少讀書山中二十年，篤於孝友。

translations.literal: In youth he read books in the mountains for twenty years and was devoted to filial piety and brotherly duty.
translations.idiomatic: He spent twenty years studying in the mountains as a young man and was known for filial devotion and brotherly loyalty.

sentences.zh: 順治十一年，舉順天鄉試，授江西廣信府推官。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Shunzhi he passed the Shuntian provincial examination and was appointed investigating censor of Guangxin Prefecture in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of Shunzhi he passed the provincial examination at Shuntian and was appointed investigating censor of Guangxin Prefecture in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 鋤強糾貪，姦宄斂戢。

translations.literal: He uprooted the powerful and corrected the greedy; villains and lawbreakers were subdued.
translations.idiomatic: He broke the power of local bullies, punished corruption, and drove villains to heel.

sentences.zh: 理讞牘，脫無罪數百人，時為語曰：「遇黎則生。

translations.literal: He handled legal documents and freed several hundred innocent persons; at the time people said: "Meet Li and live."
translations.idiomatic: Reviewing case files, he freed hundreds of innocent people. A saying spread: "Meet Li and you live."

sentences.zh: 」署玉山縣事。

translations.literal: " He was assigned to administer Yushan County.
translations.idiomatic: He was assigned to administer Yushan County.

sentences.zh: 兵后城中草三尺，不辨街巷，居民才三十二家。

translations.literal: After the wars grass in the city stood three feet high and streets could not be distinguished; residents numbered only thirty-two households.
translations.idiomatic: After the fighting, waist-high grass choked the streets of the county seat and only thirty-two households remained.

sentences.zh: 士弘立學建治，招集流亡，墾田定賦，民復舊業。

translations.literal: Shihong established schools and built up governance, gathered the displaced, opened wasteland and fixed tax assessments, and the people resumed their former occupations.
translations.idiomatic: Shihong founded schools, rebuilt local government, gathered refugees, opened fields, and fixed tax assessments until people returned to their old livelihoods.

sentences.zh: 裁缺，改授永新知縣。

translations.literal: When the post was abolished, he was reassigned as magistrate of Yongxin.
translations.idiomatic: When his post was abolished, he was reassigned as magistrate of Yongxin.

sentences.zh: 政清獄簡，與民休息。

translations.literal: His administration was clear and lawsuits few; he let the people rest.
translations.idiomatic: His government was clean, litigation light, and the people were given room to recover.

sentences.zh: 舊例，二月開徵，五月解其半。

translations.literal: By old custom, collection began in the second month and half was remitted in the fifth month.
translations.idiomatic: By custom, tax collection began in the second month and half the levy was forwarded in the fifth.

sentences.zh: 士弘陳於上官曰：「縣小民窮，二月寫租十石，貸銀一兩，三月可減至六石，四月則三石。

translations.literal: Shihong stated to his superiors: "The county is small and the people poor; in the second month registering ten piculs of rent, one tael of silver is borrowed; by the third month it can be reduced to six piculs, and in the fourth month only three piculs."
translations.idiomatic: Shihong told his superiors: "This is a small, poor county. If collection starts in the second month, tenants must pledge ten piculs of rent and borrow a tael of silver. By the third month that shrinks to six piculs, and by the fourth to three."

sentences.zh: 請以四月開徵，五月解，展兩月之徵，已為窮民留數万之糧。

translations.literal: Please begin collection in the fourth month and remit in the fifth; extending collection by two months would already leave tens of thousands of piculs of grain for the destitute people."
translations.idiomatic: Let collection begin in the fourth month and remittance follow in the fifth. Delaying two months would leave tens of thousands of piculs in the hands of the poor."

sentences.zh: 」布政使劉楗素寬仁，即允之。

translations.literal: " The provincial treasurer Liu Jian was by nature lenient and humane and at once approved it.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial Treasurer Liu Jian, a man of known kindness, approved the request at once.

sentences.zh: 甲訴乙悔婚。

translations.literal: A sued B for breaking the betrothal.
translations.idiomatic: One party sued another for breaking off a betrothal.

sentences.zh: 鄉俗婚書各裝為卷，書男女生辰。

translations.literal: By local custom marriage documents were each bound as a scroll recording the birth dates of bride and groom.
translations.idiomatic: Local custom bound marriage contracts into scrolls bearing the birth dates of bride and groom.

sentences.zh: 兩造固鄰舊，女生辰所素悉，偽為卷為證。

translations.literal: The two parties were old neighbors and he was well acquainted with the girl's birth date; he forged a scroll as evidence.
translations.idiomatic: The parties were old neighbors, so the plaintiff knew the girl's birth date well and forged a scroll as proof.

sentences.zh: 士弘先問媒證：「乙得甲聘禮若干？

translations.literal: Shihong first questioned the matchmaker and witness: "How much betrothal gift did B receive from A?"
translations.idiomatic: Shihong first questioned the matchmaker: "How much betrothal gift did the defendant receive from the plaintiff?"

sentences.zh: 行聘時有何客？

translations.literal: Who were the guests when the betrothal gifts were sent?"
translations.idiomatic: Who attended when the betrothal gifts were delivered?"

sentences.zh: 」媒證出不意，妄舉以對。

translations.literal: " The matchmaker and witness, caught off guard, answered at random.
translations.idiomatic: Caught off guard, the matchmaker invented answers on the spot.

sentences.zh: 復問甲，所對各異。

translations.literal: He questioned A again, and their answers differed.
translations.idiomatic: When he questioned the plaintiff, the stories did not match.

sentences.zh: 擘視捲軸，竹猶青，笑詰之曰：「若訂婚三載，捲軸竹色猶新，此非臨訟偽造者乎？

translations.literal: He split open the scroll and looked—the bamboo was still green; smiling he interrogated them: "If you have been betrothed three years, how can the bamboo of the scroll still be fresh? Is this not a forgery made on the eve of litigation?"
translations.idiomatic: He split the scroll open: the bamboo was still green. Smiling, he said, "You claim a betrothal of three years, yet the bamboo looks freshly cut. Was this forged for the lawsuit?"

sentences.zh: 」甲乃服罪。

translations.literal: " A then confessed guilt.
translations.idiomatic: The plaintiff confessed.

sentences.zh: 縣吏左梅伯有叔富而無子，梅伯糾賊劫殺之，獲賊而梅伯逃。

translations.literal: The county clerk Zuo Meibo had an uncle who was wealthy but childless; Meibo incited bandits to rob and kill him, the bandits were captured but Meibo fled.
translations.idiomatic: County clerk Zuo Meibo had a wealthy, childless uncle. Meibo hired bandits to rob and murder him. The bandits were caught, but Meibo escaped.

sentences.zh: 士弘抵任，叔妻哭訴，陰跡梅伯匿安福勢宦家，故緩詞曰：「此舊事。

translations.literal: When Shihong arrived at his post the uncle's wife came weeping to accuse him; he secretly traced Meibo hiding in the house of a powerful official in Anfu, and therefore spoke mildly: "This is an old matter."
translations.idiomatic: When Shihong took office, the widow came weeping to accuse Meibo. He traced Meibo secretly to the house of a powerful Anfu official and said mildly, "This is an old case."

sentences.zh: 前官不了，余安能按之？

translations.literal: The previous official could not conclude it—how can I pursue it?"
translations.idiomatic: My predecessor never closed it. How can I take it up now?"

sentences.zh: 」數月，梅伯歸，叔妻复訴，置不問。

translations.literal: " After several months Meibo returned; the uncle's wife accused again, and he set it aside without inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: Months later Meibo returned. The widow sued again, and Shihong ignored her.

sentences.zh: 梅伯且出收叔遺產，叔妻號於庭曰：「公號廉明，今寬殺人者罪，且佔寡婦田，何得為廉明！

translations.literal: Meibo then went out to collect the uncle's estate; the uncle's wife wailed in the court saying: "You are called incorrupt and clear-sighted—now you spare a murderer's crime and even seize a widow's fields; how can you be called incorrupt and clear-sighted!"
translations.idiomatic: Meibo then moved to seize the estate. The widow wailed in court: "You are praised as just, yet you spare a murderer and let him take a widow's land. What justice is this?"

sentences.zh: 」陽怒，批其牘曰：「止問田土，不問人命。

translations.literal: " He feigned anger and endorsed her petition: "Inquire only about the land, not about the life."
translations.idiomatic: He feigned anger and endorsed her petition: "Investigate the land only, not the killing."

sentences.zh: 」梅伯益自得，赴縣訴理，乃笑謂曰：「候汝三載矣！

translations.literal: " Meibo grew all the more complacent and came to the county to plead his case; Shihong then laughed and said to him: "I have waited for you three years!"
translations.idiomatic: Emboldened, Meibo came to court to claim the land. Shihong smiled and said, "I have been waiting three years for you."

sentences.zh: 」批其牘曰：「止問人命，不問田土。

translations.literal: " He endorsed the petition: "Inquire only about the life, not about the land."
translations.idiomatic: He endorsed the petition: "Investigate the killing only, not the land."

sentences.zh: 」梅伯遂伏法。

translations.literal: " Meibo then suffered the penalty of law.
translations.idiomatic: Meibo was executed.

sentences.zh: 其善斷獄多類此。

translations.literal: His skill in deciding cases was mostly of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: Many of his judgments followed this pattern.

sentences.zh: 考最，擢陝西甘州同知。

translations.literal: Rated highest in evaluation, he was promoted to subprefect of Ganzhou in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Rated at the top of his evaluation, he was promoted to subprefect of Ganzhou in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 复考最，擢江南常州知府。

translations.literal: Again rated highest, he was promoted to prefect of Changzhou in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Rated highest again, he was promoted to prefect of Changzhou in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 吳三桂亂起，關隴震動，大吏疏請擢洮西道副使，未到官而洮、岷陷。

translations.literal: When Wu Sangui's rebellion arose, Guanlong was shaken; the high officials memorialized requesting his promotion to Vice Commissioner of the Taoxi Circuit, but before he reached office Tao and Min fell.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Sangui rebelled, the Guanlong region was thrown into turmoil. Senior officials memorialized to promote him to Vice Commissioner of the Taoxi Circuit, but before he could take up the post, Tao and Min had fallen.

sentences.zh: 邊外群番乘亂內犯，肆剽掠，調署甘山道。

translations.literal: Tribal groups beyond the border took advantage of the chaos to invade inward and plunder at will; he was transferred to act as Ganshan Circuit commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Border tribes raided inward amid the chaos, and he was reassigned to act as commissioner of the Ganshan Circuit.

sentences.zh: 王輔臣叛，河東失守。

translations.literal: Wang Fuchen rebelled and Hedong was lost.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Fuchen rebelled, the east bank of the river was lost.

sentences.zh: 士弘以兵集當謀帥，言於巡撫，謂：「恢復河東，非用河西兵不可；

translations.literal: Shihong, seeing troops gathered, said a commander must be chosen and told the governor: "To recover Hedong, troops from west of the river cannot be dispensed with;"
translations.idiomatic: With armies massing, Shihong told the governor that a commander was needed: "Recovering the east bank will require troops from west of the river;"

sentences.zh: 用河西兵，非責之提督張勇不可。

translations.literal: "to use troops from west of the river, none but Regional Commander Zhang Yong can be charged with the task."
translations.idiomatic: "and only Regional Commander Zhang Yong can lead them."

sentences.zh: 」疏入，授勇靖逆將軍，節制諸鎮。

translations.literal: " When the memorial entered, Yong was appointed Pacifier of Rebellion General and given command over all garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was approved. Zhang Yong was appointed Pacifier of Rebellion General with authority over all garrisons.

sentences.zh: 复蘭州，士弘贊畫功為多。

translations.literal: When Lanzhou was recovered, Shihong's merit in planning was greatest.
translations.idiomatic: When Lanzhou was recovered, Shihong's planning counted for much of the success.

sentences.zh: 署甘肅按察使，按失守官吏罪，務平允。

translations.literal: He acted as Gansu Provincial Surveillance Commissioner and investigated the crimes of officials who had lost their posts, striving for fairness.
translations.idiomatic: Acting as Gansu Surveillance Commissioner, he tried officials who had lost their posts, always seeking fair judgment.

sentences.zh: 寧夏兵叛，殺提督陳福，調寧夏道。

translations.literal: The Ningxia troops rebelled and killed Regional Commander Chen Fu; he was transferred to the Ningxia Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: When the Ningxia garrison mutinied and killed Regional Commander Chen Fu, Shihong was transferred to the Ningxia Circuit.

sentences.zh: 嚴守禦，安反側，免衛所逋糧七萬五千石。

translations.literal: He defended strictly, settled those wavering in loyalty, and remitted seventy-five thousand piculs of grain arrears owed by military colonies.
translations.idiomatic: He tightened defenses, calmed wavering loyalties, and remitted seventy-five thousand piculs of grain arrears owed by the garrison colonies.

sentences.zh: 康熙十六年，寇平，以功進布政使參議。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Kangxi the rebels were pacified, and for his merit he was promoted to Administrative Supervisor in the provincial treasury.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year of Kangxi, after the rebels were suppressed, he was promoted to Administrative Supervisor in the provincial treasury for his service.

sentences.zh: 母老乞歸，家居幾三十年。

translations.literal: His mother was old and he begged to return home; he dwelt at home for nearly thirty years.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother grew old he asked to retire and lived at home for nearly thirty years.

sentences.zh: 卒，年八十。

translations.literal: He died at the age of eighty.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of eighty.

sentences.zh: 士弘備兵甘山時，取晉辛憲英語：「軍旅之間可以濟者，惟仁與恕。

translations.literal: When Shihong was preparing troops on Ganshan, he took a saying of Jin Xin Xianying: "In military affairs what can avail is only benevolence and forbearance."
translations.idiomatic: While Shihong was organizing troops on Ganshan, he took a line from Jin-dynasty Xin Xianying: "In war, only benevolence and forbearance can carry the day."

sentences.zh: 」因以名其堂。

translations.literal: " He therefore named his hall accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: He named his hall after that saying.

sentences.zh: 多弘安，字君修，直隸阜城人。

translations.literal: Duo Hong'an, courtesy name Junxiu, was a man of Fucheng in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: Duo Hong'an, whose courtesy name was Junxiu, came from Fucheng in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 順治五年，選拔貢生。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Shunzhi he was selected as a tribute student by special examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Shunzhi he was selected as a tribute student by special examination.

sentences.zh: 康熙初，授廣東靈山知縣。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kangxi he was appointed magistrate of Lingshan in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kangxi reign he was appointed magistrate of Lingshan in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 兵後荒殘，居無衙舍。

translations.literal: After the wars the region was desolate and ruined, and he had no yamen in which to dwell.
translations.idiomatic: The county lay in ruins after the fighting, and there was no government office for him to occupy.

sentences.zh: 弘安請免積年逋賦，招撫流移，捐給牛種，民得安耕稼。

translations.literal: Hong'an requested remission of accumulated tax arrears, offered amnesty and settlement to the displaced, donated oxen and seed, and the people were able to farm in peace.
translations.idiomatic: Hong'an secured remission of years of tax arrears, brought back refugees, and donated oxen and seed until the people could farm again in peace.

sentences.zh: 葺城垣，創學宮，繕官廨，捕除盜賊，靈山大治，士民刊石紀其績。

translations.literal: He repaired the city walls, founded a school, renovated official buildings, captured and eliminated bandits; Lingshan was greatly ordered, and gentry and people carved stone to record his achievements.
translations.idiomatic: He rebuilt the walls, founded a school, restored government buildings, and stamped out banditry until Lingshan prospered again. The gentry and people set up a stone monument to his work.

sentences.zh: 七年，遷奉天承德知縣。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was transferred to magistrate of Chengde in Fengtian.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was transferred to magistrate of Chengde in Fengtian.

sentences.zh: 旗、民抗法者，送部懲治，皆懾服。

translations.literal: Bannermen and commoners who resisted the law were sent to the ministry for punishment, and all were cowed into submission.
translations.idiomatic: Bannermen and commoners who defied the law were sent to the ministry for punishment, and all submitted in fear.

sentences.zh: 十年，擢陝西延安靖邊同知。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was promoted to subprefect of Jingbian in Yan'an, Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was promoted to subprefect of Jingbian in Yan'an, Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 十六年，補江南淮安山盱河務同知。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he was appointed to fill the post of subprefect for the Shanxu River works at Huai'an in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he was appointed subprefect in charge of the Shanxu River works at Huai'an in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 時高堰長堤潰決，淮水注寶應、高郵，不復出清口敵黃。

translations.literal: At that time the long embankment of the Gaoyan dam burst; the Huai River poured into Baoying and Gaoyou and no longer issued from Qingkou to contend with the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: The long embankment of the Gaoyan dam had burst. The Huai poured into Baoying and Gaoyou and no longer met the Yellow River at Qingkou.

sentences.zh: 黃水直注里河，運道淤淺，复隨淮入堰，無由會清口下云梯關入海，近海口盡淤墊。

translations.literal: Yellow River water poured straight into the inner channel; the transport route silted shallow, again following the Huai into the dam, with no way to join Qingkou and descend through Yunti Pass to the sea; near the estuary all was silted and choked.
translations.idiomatic: Yellow River water flooded the inner channel, the transport route silted up, and the Huai was forced back into the dam. The route to Qingkou and down through Yunti Pass to the sea was blocked, and the estuary was choked with silt.

sentences.zh: 弘安與河督靳輔籌策築高堰，束淮敵黃，治爛泥淺諸故道，導清水入里河，運道乃通。

translations.literal: Hong'an and the river commissioner Jin Fu planned to build the Gaoyan dam, confine the Huai to contend with the Yellow River, repair the old channels of Lanni and Qian, and lead clear water into the inner channel, and the transport route was opened.
translations.idiomatic: Hong'an and River Commissioner Jin Fu planned the Gaoyan dam to hold the Huai against the Yellow River, cleared the old Lanni and Qian channels, and directed clear water into the inner channel until the transport route was open again.

sentences.zh: 修築兩岸及河口清江大閘，與淮工相表裡。

translations.literal: He built up both banks and the great Qingjiang sluice at the estuary, complementing the Huai River works.
translations.idiomatic: He strengthened both banks and built the great Qingjiang sluice at the estuary, works that complemented the Huai River project.

sentences.zh: 清河達雲梯關數百里，葭葦榛蕪，壅塞故道。

translations.literal: The clear channel extended several hundred li to Yunti Pass, overgrown with reeds and rushes, choking the old route.
translations.idiomatic: For hundreds of li from the clear channel to Yunti Pass, reeds and brush choked the old waterway.

sentences.zh: 用以水攻沙法，塞周橋、高澗諸閘，使清淮無旁洩，蓄全力攻積沙。

translations.literal: He applied the method of using water to attack sand, blocked the sluices at Zhouqiao, Gaojian, and elsewhere, so that the clear Huai had no side leakage and stored full force to attack accumulated sand.
translations.idiomatic: He used the method of scouring sand with water, closed the Zhouqiao and Gaojian sluices, and kept the clear Huai from leaking sideways so its full force could scour the accumulated silt.

sentences.zh: 十七年，大雨，淮盛漲，與黃併入海。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year heavy rain fell; the Huai swelled greatly and together with the Yellow River entered the sea.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year, after heavy rains, the Huai rose high and carried the Yellow River with it into the sea.

sentences.zh: 治淮、治黃、治運，並收成效。

translations.literal: Managing the Huai, managing the Yellow River, and managing transport all achieved results together.
translations.idiomatic: Control of the Huai, the Yellow River, and the transport route all succeeded together.

sentences.zh: 十九年，擢淮安知府。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he was promoted to prefect of Huai'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year he was promoted to prefect of Huai'an.

sentences.zh: 二十年，擢淮揚道。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he was promoted to the Huai-Yang Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year he was promoted to commissioner of the Huai-Yang Circuit.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，擢安徽按察使。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he was promoted to Anhui Provincial Surveillance Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year he was promoted to Anhui Surveillance Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 時方議浚下河、治高堰。

translations.literal: At that time they were debating dredging the lower river and repairing the Gaoyan dam.
translations.idiomatic: The court was then debating whether to dredge the lower river and repair the Gaoyan dam.

sentences.zh: 弘安入覲，疏陳：「高堰宜急治，無論下河開浚與否。

translations.literal: Hong'an entered audience and memorialized: "The Gaoyan dam should be repaired urgently, regardless of whether the lower river is dredged or not."
translations.idiomatic: When Hong'an presented himself at court, he memorialized: "The Gaoyan dam must be repaired at once, whether or not the lower river is dredged."

sentences.zh: 治堰法，砌石先安地釘，湖底水深，費帑甚繁。

translations.literal: In repairing the dam, laying stone requires first setting ground nails; the lake bottom is deep in water, and expenditures from the treasury are very heavy.
translations.idiomatic: The usual method of stone facing requires ground nails driven first. The lake bed is deep, and the cost is enormous.

sentences.zh: 如用板若掃，水勢盪掣，尤易摧殘。

translations.literal: If boards or fascines are used, the water's force surges and pulls, and they are especially easily destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Boards or fascines are worse still: the surge of water tears them apart all the more easily.

sentences.zh: 惟密釘排椿，內實以碎石，庶可敵風浪，省金錢。

translations.literal: Only by driving rows of piles closely and filling them within with broken stone can one hope to withstand wind and waves and save money.
translations.idiomatic: Only close rows of piles packed with rubble within can stand against wind and waves and save money.

sentences.zh: 十餘年後，黃河刷深，則湖、河水俱卑，高堰既固，下河亦漸就理。

translations.literal: After more than ten years the Yellow River will scour deeper, then lake and river waters will both be lower; once the Gaoyan dam is firm, the lower river will also gradually be put in order.
translations.idiomatic: In ten years or more the Yellow River will scour deeper, lake and river levels will fall, the Gaoyan dam will hold firm, and the lower river will gradually come right.

sentences.zh: 」二十八年，遷江西布政使，乞歸。

translations.literal: " In the twenty-eighth year he was transferred to Jiangxi Provincial Treasurer and begged to return home.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year he was made Jiangxi Provincial Treasurer and asked to retire.

sentences.zh: 後值黃、運兩河潰溢，起用弘安。

translations.literal: Later when the Yellow River and transport river both burst and overflowed, Hong'an was recalled to service.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the Yellow River and the transport canal both burst their banks, Hong'an was called back into service.

sentences.zh: 會病卒，祀靈山名宦。

translations.literal: He happened to fall ill and die; he was enshrined among the notable officials of Lingshan.
translations.idiomatic: He fell ill and died before he could finish. Lingshan enshrined him among its notable officials.

sentences.zh: 佟國聘，字君莘，奉天人。

translations.literal: Tong Guopin, courtesy name Junxin, was a man of Fengtian.
translations.idiomatic: Tong Guopin, whose courtesy name was Junxin, came from Fengtian.

sentences.zh: 以廕生補吏部筆帖式。

translations.literal: As a yinsheng he was appointed a clerk in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Through hereditary privilege he entered the Ministry of Personnel as a clerk.

sentences.zh: 康熙十年，授江南碭山知縣，縣當黃河衝，研求治河方略。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Kangxi he was appointed magistrate of Dangshan in Jiangnan; the county lay in the path of the Yellow River, and he studied methods of river control.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Kangxi he was appointed magistrate of Dangshan in Jiangnan. The county lay in the Yellow River's path, and he devoted himself to studying river control.

sentences.zh: 擢歸仁堤同知，調宿桃同知。

translations.literal: He was promoted to subprefect of the Guiren embankment and transferred to subprefect of Sutao.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to subprefect of the Guiren embankment and later transferred to subprefect of Sutao.

sentences.zh: 擢貴州平遠知府，河督靳輔疏留任，十餘年倚如左右手。

translations.literal: He was promoted to prefect of Pingyuan in Guizhou; River Commissioner Jin Fu memorialized to retain him in office, and for more than ten years relied on him as on right hand and left.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to prefect of Pingyuan in Guizhou, but River Commissioner Jin Fu memorialized to keep him. For more than ten years Jin Fu relied on him as his right hand.

sentences.zh: 塞楊家莊、蕭家渡決口，建硃家堂、溫家廟二石壩，浚白洋引河九道，築黃河南、北兩岸堤，浚中河，靡役不從。

translations.literal: He closed the breaches at Yangjiazhuang and Xiaojiadu, built the two stone dams at Zhujiatang and Wenjiamiao, dredged nine channels of the Baiyang diversion river, constructed embankments on both south and north banks of the Yellow River, dredged the middle river—no task did he not follow through on.
translations.idiomatic: He closed the breaches at Yangjiazhuang and Xiaojiadu, built stone dams at Zhujiatang and Wenjiamiao, dredged nine channels of the Baiyang diversion, raised embankments on both banks of the Yellow River, and cleared the middle river. No project was left undone.

sentences.zh: 久之，擢山東濟寧道副使。

translations.literal: After a long time he was promoted to Vice Commissioner of the Jining Circuit in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Eventually he was promoted to Vice Commissioner of the Jining Circuit in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 道地為漕運樞紐，卹夫役，減苛稅，除冗費，能舉其職。

translations.literal: The circuit territory was the hub of grain transport; he showed compassion to laborers, reduced harsh taxes, eliminated redundant expenses, and was able to fulfill his duties.
translations.idiomatic: The circuit was the hub of the grain transport system. He eased the burden on laborers, cut harsh taxes, eliminated waste, and discharged his duties well.

sentences.zh: 復調監督高堰工程。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to supervise the Gaoyan dam works.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned to supervise the Gaoyan dam project.

sentences.zh: 三十八年，卒於官。

translations.literal: In the thirty-eighth year he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-eighth year he died in office.

sentences.zh: 王繻，字慎夫，河南睢州人。

translations.literal: Wang Xu, courtesy name Shenfu, was a man of Suizhou in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xu, whose courtesy name was Shenfu, came from Suizhou in Henan.

sentences.zh: 少學於湯斌。

translations.literal: In youth he studied under Tang Bin.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he studied under Tang Bin.

sentences.zh: 康熙二十五年，以歲貢生授直隸東明知縣。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year of Kangxi, as a annual tribute student he was appointed magistrate of Dongming in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year of Kangxi he was appointed magistrate of Dongming in Zhili as a tribute student.

sentences.zh: 糧賦多欺隱，易甲長，大戶使族長督之，飛灑不行，流亡來歸。

translations.literal: Grain taxes involved much concealment and fraud; he replaced the village heads, had large households supervised by clan heads, stopped the practice of shifting tax burdens, and refugees returned.
translations.idiomatic: Grain taxes were widely concealed. He replaced village heads, had large households supervised by clan elders, ended tax-shifting abuses, and refugees began to return.

sentences.zh: 民間養官馬為累，力除之。

translations.literal: Among the people raising official horses was a burden; he strove to abolish it.
translations.idiomatic: The people were burdened by the duty of raising official horses, and he abolished the practice.

sentences.zh: 撫盜魁，責以緝捕，盜絕跡。

translations.literal: He won over bandit chiefs and charged them with hunting down bandits; bandits vanished without trace.
translations.idiomatic: He won over bandit chiefs and charged them with hunting down their fellows until banditry disappeared.

sentences.zh: 逃人誣攀良民，雪之。

translations.literal: Fugitives falsely implicated innocent people; he cleared them.
translations.idiomatic: When fugitives falsely implicated innocent people, he cleared their names.

sentences.zh: 民有繼妻素淫，欲並亂前妻女，不從，戕之死。

translations.literal: A man had a stepmother who was by nature licentious; she wished to debauch together the daughter of the former wife, who refused, and she killed her.
translations.idiomatic: A man's stepmother, who was notoriously licentious, tried to force herself on his daughter by a previous wife. When the girl refused, the stepmother killed her.

sentences.zh: 繻謂母道絕，當故殺妻前夫子律論斬，報可，因著為例。

translations.literal: Xu said the maternal way was severed and she should be sentenced to decapitation under the statute for deliberate killing of a wife's child by a former husband; the reply approved it, and it was established as a precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Xu held that she had severed all maternal duty and should be sentenced under the statute for killing a stepchild. The court approved, and the ruling became a precedent.

sentences.zh: 母憂去，服闋，補獲鹿。

translations.literal: He left on his mother's mourning, and when mourning ended was appointed to Huolu.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to mourn his mother and, when mourning ended, was appointed to Huolu.

sentences.zh: 治驛有法，民不累於供億。

translations.literal: He managed the courier stations with method, and the people were not burdened by supply obligations.
translations.idiomatic: He ran the courier stations efficiently, and the people were not burdened by supply duties.

sentences.zh: 內遷戶部員外郎，擢郎中。

translations.literal: He was transferred within the capital to vice director in the Ministry of Revenue and promoted to director.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to the capital as a vice director in the Ministry of Revenue and later promoted to director.

sentences.zh: 三十八年，出為江南糧儲道。

translations.literal: In the thirty-eighth year he went out as Grain Storage Commissioner of Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-eighth year he was appointed Grain Storage Commissioner of Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 道舊有倉規銀鉅萬，繻一擯勿取。

translations.literal: The commissioner's office had long had tens of thousands in customary granary fees; Xu rejected them all and would not take them.
translations.idiomatic: The office had long collected tens of thousands in customary granary fees. Xu refused every penny.

sentences.zh: 將徵漕，扁舟行縣，懲其濫收者。

translations.literal: When the grain transport levy was about to be collected, he went by small boat through the counties and punished those who collected excessively.
translations.idiomatic: Before the grain transport levy was collected, he toured the counties in a small boat and punished officials who overcharged.

sentences.zh: 至宜興，宜興民曰：「吾民四十年不見糧道，今飛來耶？

translations.literal: When he reached Yixing, the people of Yixing said: "Our people have not seen the grain commissioner for forty years—has he flown here today?"
translations.idiomatic: At Yixing the people said, "We have not seen a grain commissioner in forty years. Has one flown in today?"

sentences.zh: 」號曰「飛糧道」。

translations.literal: " They called him the "Flying Grain Commissioner."
translations.idiomatic: They nicknamed him the Flying Grain Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 道庫歲收銀八十五萬兩，為修船及弁丁運費。

translations.literal: The commissioner's treasury collected eight hundred fifty thousand taels of silver yearly for repairing boats and transport costs of runners and boatmen.
translations.idiomatic: The commissioner's treasury took in 850,000 taels a year for ship repairs and transport costs.

sentences.zh: 運丁預支行糧，例扣月息，丁益困，繻悉罷之。

translations.literal: Transport workers received grain advances and by custom monthly interest was deducted; the workers grew ever more distressed, and Xu abolished all of this.
translations.idiomatic: Transport workers received grain advances with monthly interest deducted by custom, which left them ever poorer. Xu abolished the practice entirely.

sentences.zh: 四十年，擢江蘇按察使。

translations.literal: In the fortieth year he was promoted to Jiangsu Provincial Surveillance Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the fortieth year he was promoted to Jiangsu Surveillance Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 治獄仁恕，多所平反。

translations.literal: In handling cases he was benevolent and forgiving, and reversed many wrongful convictions.
translations.idiomatic: He handled cases with mercy and reversed many wrongful convictions.

sentences.zh: 宿州生攜妻子出客授，妻兄女來視，居數日，妻子併中毒死，妻兄素有隙，疑其女置毒，告官，被刑誣服。

translations.literal: A scholar of Suzhou took wife and children out to teach as a guest tutor; his wife's brother's daughter came to visit, and after several days wife and children together died of poison; the wife's brother had long borne a grudge and suspected his daughter had placed the poison; he reported to officials, and under torture she falsely confessed.
translations.idiomatic: A Suzhou scholar took his family to teach abroad. His wife's niece came to visit, and within days wife and children died of poison. The wife's brother, who bore a grudge, accused his daughter. Under torture she confessed falsely.

sentences.zh: 繻疑之，問其室來往復何人，得十二歲學徒畏師嚴置鏚食中狀，事乃白。

translations.literal: Xu doubted this and asked who else came and went in the house; he obtained testimony that a twelve-year-old student, fearing his teacher's severity, had placed arsenic in the food, and the matter was cleared.
translations.idiomatic: Xu had doubts and asked who else visited the house. He learned that a twelve-year-old student, fearing his teacher's harshness, had put arsenic in the food. The truth came out.

sentences.zh: 無錫民毆攻皮匠，匠死，僧與民仇，證為鬥毆殺。

translations.literal: A man of Wuxi beat a leather worker; the worker died. A monk bore a grudge against the man and testified that he had killed him in a brawl.
translations.idiomatic: A Wuxi man beat a leather worker to death. A monk who hated the man testified that it was murder in a brawl.

sentences.zh: 繻察鬥毆日月在保辜限外，詰曰：「傷重何不醫？

translations.literal: Xu observed that the date of the brawl fell outside the period of limited liability for wounds; he interrogated: "If the injury was severe, why was no doctor called?"
translations.idiomatic: Xu noted that the brawl fell outside the statutory period for liability for wounds. He asked, "If the injury was serious, why was no doctor summoned?"

sentences.zh: 」出醫方，則匠死於傷寒，僧乃服。

translations.literal: " When the medical prescription was produced, it showed the worker died of cold damage; the monk then confessed.
translations.idiomatic: The prescription showed the worker had died of typhoid fever, and the monk confessed.

sentences.zh: 上南巡，入覲，顧宋犖曰：「朕聞繻督糧時官聲甚好。

translations.literal: When the emperor made a southern tour, Xu entered audience; the emperor turned to Song Luo and said: "I have heard that when Xu supervised grain his official reputation was very good."
translations.idiomatic: During an imperial southern tour, Xu presented himself at court. The emperor turned to Song Luo and said, "I hear Xu had an excellent reputation when he supervised grain transport."

sentences.zh: 」時繻已病，遣御醫視之，賜德里雅噶藥一器，溫旨慰諭，复賜御書。

translations.literal: " At that time Xu was already ill; the emperor sent an imperial physician to see him, bestowed a vessel of deliyaga medicine, comforted him with warm words, and again granted imperial calligraphy.
translations.idiomatic: Xu was already ill. The emperor sent an imperial physician, gave him a dose of court medicine, spoke words of comfort, and bestowed imperial calligraphy.

sentences.zh: 繻曰：「按察任大責重，臥治即辜恩。

translations.literal: Xu said: "The surveillance commissioner's post bears great responsibility; to govern from bed is to fail the emperor's grace."
translations.idiomatic: Xu replied, "The surveillance commissioner's post carries heavy responsibility. To govern from my sickbed would betray the emperor's grace."

sentences.zh: 」引疾歸，年甫五十。

translations.literal: " He cited illness and returned home, having just reached fifty years.
translations.idiomatic: He pleaded illness and retired at the age of fifty.

sentences.zh: 久之，卒於家。

translations.literal: After a long time he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home some years later.

sentences.zh: 田呈瑞，字介璞，山西汾陽人。

translations.literal: Tian Chengrui, courtesy name Jiepu, was a man of Fenyang in Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Chengrui, whose courtesy name was Jiepu, came from Fenyang in Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 康熙中，仕為中書舍人。

translations.literal: During Kangxi he served as a secretary in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kangxi reign he served as a secretariat draftsman.

sentences.zh: 出襄南河事。

translations.literal: He went out to manage the Xiangnan River works.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out to manage the Xiangnan River works.

sentences.zh: 有堤當水沖，曰：「此堤一壞，萬家其魚矣！

translations.literal: There was an embankment facing the rush of water; he said: "If this embankment breaks once, ten thousand households will be fish in the net!"
translations.idiomatic: An embankment stood in the direct path of the current. He warned, "If this dike fails, ten thousand households will be ruined!"

sentences.zh: 土堤易修易敗，宜更以石。

translations.literal: An earthen embankment is easy to repair and easy to fail; it should be replaced with stone.
translations.idiomatic: An earthen dike is easy to repair and easy to lose. It should be rebuilt in stone.

sentences.zh: 」家素豐，出私錢成之。

translations.literal: " His family had long been wealthy, and he paid from private funds to complete it.
translations.idiomatic: His family was wealthy, and he paid for the work out of his own funds.

sentences.zh: 以功擢大名道，未之任，調陝西臨洮道。

translations.literal: For his merit he was promoted to the Daming Circuit, but before taking office was transferred to the Lintao Circuit in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: For this work he was promoted to the Daming Circuit, but before taking office he was transferred to the Lintao Circuit in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 遇飢治賑，策馬行郡縣山谷間，豪右胥吏不敢為奸弊。

translations.literal: When famine came he managed relief, riding his horse through the valleys among prefectures and counties; powerful families and clerks did not dare commit fraud.
translations.idiomatic: During a famine he organized relief, riding through the mountain valleys of the prefecture. Local magnates and clerks dared not cheat.

sentences.zh: 呈瑞念救荒無善策，於蘭州西石佛灣鑿渠，教民造水車，引以溉田，歲增粟十餘萬石，民為建生祠。

translations.literal: Chengrui reflected that famine relief had no good method; west of Lanzhou at Shifo Bay he cut a canal, taught the people to build water wheels, and led water to irrigate fields; grain increased by more than one hundred thousand piculs yearly, and the people built a living shrine to him.
translations.idiomatic: Convinced that famine relief had no lasting answer, Chengrui cut a canal at Shifo Bay west of Lanzhou, taught the people to build water wheels, and irrigated the fields. Grain yields rose by more than a hundred thousand piculs a year, and the people built a shrine to him.

sentences.zh: 調浙江金衢嚴道，署糧儲道，徵漕積弊盡洗滌之。

translations.literal: He was transferred to the Jinhua-Quzhou-Yanzhou Circuit in Zhejiang, acted as Grain Storage Commissioner, and washed away all accumulated abuses in the grain transport levy.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to the Jinhua-Quzhou-Yanzhou Circuit in Zhejiang, served as acting Grain Storage Commissioner, and swept away every abuse in the grain transport levy.

sentences.zh: 值旱，冒暑省荒，感疾，乞歸不得。

translations.literal: When drought came he braved the heat to inspect famine areas, fell ill, and begged to return but was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: During a drought he braved the heat to inspect stricken areas, fell ill, and asked to retire but was refused.

sentences.zh: 五十九年，卒於官。

translations.literal: In the fifty-ninth year he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-ninth year he died in office.

sentences.zh: 張孟球，字夔石，江南長洲人。

translations.literal: Zhang Mengqiu, courtesy name Kuishi, was a man of Changzhou in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Mengqiu, whose courtesy name was Kuishi, came from Changzhou in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 康熙二十四年進士，授山東昌樂知縣。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year of Kangxi he became a jinshi and was appointed magistrate of Changle in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the twenty-fourth year of Kangxi and was appointed magistrate of Changle in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 入為工部主事。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as a principal clerk in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was called to the capital as a principal clerk in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 累遷禮部郎中。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to director in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through several posts to director in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 出督雲南學政，父​​憂去，服闋，補福建糧驛道。

translations.literal: He went out as educational commissioner of Yunnan, left on his father's mourning, and when mourning ended was appointed to the Fujian Grain and Courier Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He served as educational commissioner of Yunnan, left to mourn his father, and after mourning was appointed to the Fujian Grain and Courier Circuit.

sentences.zh: 駐防軍食取給於漕。

translations.literal: The garrison troops' food was supplied from the grain transport.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison's rations came from the grain transport system.

sentences.zh: 上游四郡阻灘險。

translations.literal: The four upstream prefectures were blocked by shoals and perilous currents.
translations.idiomatic: The four upstream prefectures were blocked by shoals and dangerous currents.

sentences.zh: 故事，徵解折色，官為採置，輒抑勒病商。

translations.literal: By precedent, collection was made in commuted silver and officials purchased supplies, invariably squeezing and harming merchants.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent the levy was collected in commuted silver and officials made the purchases, invariably squeezing merchants.

sentences.zh: 孟球於延、建產米地平價購米，僦民船運省城，不假吏胥，諸弊盡絕。

translations.literal: Mengqiu bought rice at fair price in the rice-producing lands of Yanping and Jianning, hired civilian boats to transport it to the provincial capital, used no clerks, and all abuses were ended.
translations.idiomatic: Mengqiu bought rice at fair prices in Yanping and Jianning, hired civilian boats to carry it to the provincial capital without using clerks, and ended every abuse.

sentences.zh: 地多山嶺，官吏濫用驛夫，孟球禁革私冒。

translations.literal: The region had many mountains and ridges; officials abused courier laborers, and Mengqiu forbade and abolished private imposts.
translations.idiomatic: The region was mountainous, and officials abused courier labor. Mengqiu banned private imposts on the courier system.

sentences.zh: 遇大徭，預期發僱值，終其任無擾驛者。

translations.literal: When great corvée labor came due, he issued hire payments in advance, and throughout his term no courier laborers were disturbed.
translations.idiomatic: When major corvée duties fell due, he paid hire wages in advance, and throughout his term the courier system was left undisturbed.

sentences.zh: 調河南糧儲道。

translations.literal: He was transferred to the Henan Grain Storage Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to the Henan Grain Storage Circuit.

sentences.zh: 河南漕糧，就衛輝水次收兌。

translations.literal: Henan's transport grain was received and exchanged at the Weihui landing.
translations.idiomatic: Henan's transport grain was received and exchanged at the Weihui landing.

sentences.zh: 舊無倉廒，又無額役，運船調之他省。

translations.literal: Formerly there were no granaries, nor allotted labor, and transport boats were reassigned to other provinces.
translations.idiomatic: There had been no granaries and no allotted labor; transport boats were reassigned to other provinces.

sentences.zh: 天寒水涸，糧不時至，宿河干以待，遇雨雪則米濕霉變，又患盜竊。

translations.literal: When the weather turned cold and waters dried up, grain did not arrive on time; they lodged on the riverbank to wait, and when rain or snow came the rice grew damp and moldy, while theft was also a worry.
translations.idiomatic: In cold weather when the rivers ran low, grain shipments were delayed. Boats waited on the dry riverbank, grain spoiled in rain and snow, and theft was constant.

sentences.zh: 孟球始以羨餘建倉。

translations.literal: Mengqiu first used surplus funds to build granaries.
translations.idiomatic: Mengqiu used surplus funds to build granaries for the first time.

sentences.zh: 署布政使。

translations.literal: He acted as Provincial Treasurer.
translations.idiomatic: He served as acting Provincial Treasurer.

sentences.zh: 西藏用兵，調河南馬騾萬，凡騾馬三需一夫，剋期兩月。

translations.literal: When troops were used in Tibet, ten thousand horses and mules were levied from Henan; for every three pack animals one man was required, with a deadline of two months.
translations.idiomatic: When war broke out in Tibet, Henan was ordered to supply ten thousand horses and mules, with one handler for every three animals, all within two months.

sentences.zh: 孟球止宿郊外，躬自檢閱，西路近陝諸郡遣吏往督之，盡除需索留難諸弊。

translations.literal: Mengqiu lodged in the suburbs, personally inspected the animals, sent officials to supervise the western route and nearby Shaanxi prefectures, and eliminated all abuses of demands, delays, and obstruction.
translations.idiomatic: Mengqiu camped in the suburbs and inspected the animals himself. He sent officials to supervise the western route and the Shaanxi border counties and eliminated every abuse of extortion and delay.

sentences.zh: 凡五十四日，馬驢如數遣赴軍，而民不擾。

translations.literal: In fifty-four days the horses and mules were dispatched to the army in full number, and the people were not disturbed.
translations.idiomatic: Within fifty-four days the full quota reached the army, and the people were left unharmed.

sentences.zh: 擢按察使。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Surveillance Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Surveillance Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 蘭陽民硃復業附白蓮教，自稱明裔，煽惑數縣。

translations.literal: A man of Lanyang, Zhu Fuye, joined the White Lotus teaching, called himself a descendant of the Ming, and incited several counties.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Fuye of Lanyang joined the White Lotus sect, claimed descent from the Ming house, and stirred up several counties.

sentences.zh: 孟球檄杞縣知縣寧君佐馳往捕治，盡獲其黨。

translations.literal: Mengqiu dispatched an order to Qi County magistrate Ning Junzuo to hurry and arrest them; all their party were captured.
translations.idiomatic: Mengqiu ordered Qi County magistrate Ning Junzuo to ride out at once and arrest the conspirators. The whole band was taken.

sentences.zh: 上命尚書張廷樞往按，從孟球議，誅其與逆謀者，愚民被誘悉釋之。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Minister Zhang Tingshu to investigate on the spot; following Mengqiu's proposal, those who joined the rebellion plot were executed, and foolish people who had been enticed were all released.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Minister Zhang Tingshu to investigate. Following Mengqiu's advice, those who had joined the plot were executed, and the common people who had been misled were all released.

sentences.zh: 淅川營兵博，知縣崔錫執而罪之，兵譁，執南陽知府沈淵，眾辱之，總兵高成不能治。

translations.literal: A soldier of the Xichuan garrison gambled; magistrate Cui Xi arrested and punished him; the troops mutinied, seized Nanyang prefect Shen Yuan, and publicly humiliated him; Regional Commander Gao Cheng could not control them.
translations.idiomatic: A soldier of the Xichuan garrison gambled. Magistrate Cui Xi arrested and punished him, and the troops mutinied. They seized Nanyang Prefect Shen Yuan and publicly humiliated him. Regional Commander Gao Cheng could not restore order.

sentences.zh: 時巡撫張聖佐坐譴，孟球護巡撫，曰：「南陽地連襄、鄖，急則鋌而走險，事未可知。

translations.literal: At that time Governor Zhang Shengzuo was under censure; Mengqiu shielded the governor and said: "Nanyang borders Xiangyang and Yun; pressed hard, they may take desperate risks—the outcome cannot be known."
translations.idiomatic: Governor Zhang Shengzuo was then under censure. Mengqiu shielded him and warned, "Nanyang borders Xiangyang and Yun. Push too hard and desperate men may turn to violence. The outcome is uncertain."

sentences.zh: 」密令附近諸縣嚴守禦，諭：「止誅首惡，自首免罪。

translations.literal: " He secretly ordered nearby counties to defend strictly and proclaimed: "Punish only the ringleaders; those who surrender themselves are exempt from guilt."
translations.idiomatic: He secretly ordered the neighboring counties to tighten their defenses and proclaimed, "Execute only the ringleaders. Those who surrender will be spared."

sentences.zh: 」得倡亂者七人誅之，不數日而事定。

translations.literal: " Seven who had instigated the disorder were seized and executed; within a few days the affair was settled.
translations.idiomatic: Seven ringleaders were captured and executed, and within days the disturbance was over.

sentences.zh: 康熙末，乞歸，不復出。

translations.literal: At the end of Kangxi he begged to return home and did not come forth again.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Kangxi reign he asked to retire and never took office again.

sentences.zh: 乾隆初，卒，年八十。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qianlong he died at the age of eighty.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Qianlong reign he died at the age of eighty.

sentences.zh: 論曰：官監司卓卓有名氏，即平進至督撫，易耳。

translations.literal: The commentary says: Officials among circuit intendants who stand out with famous names could easily advance by routine promotion to governor-general or governor.
translations.idiomatic: The commentators say: Circuit officials of outstanding reputation could easily have risen by routine promotion to governor or governor-general.

sentences.zh: 如紫綬等皆早退，遂以監司終。

translations.literal: Men such as Zishou all retired early and thus ended their careers as circuit officials.
translations.idiomatic: Men such as Zishou retired early and ended their careers at the circuit level.

sentences.zh: 紫綬崎嶇兵間，捍偏隅為民保障；

translations.literal: Zishou struggled through the hardships of war, defending a remote corner as a bulwark for the people;
translations.idiomatic: Zishou held a desperate frontier through years of war and shielded the people in a remote corner;

sentences.zh: 州佐、士弘勤勤重民事；

translations.literal: Zhouzuo and Shihong diligently attended to the people's affairs;
translations.idiomatic: Zhouzuo and Shihong devoted themselves tirelessly to the people's welfare;

sentences.zh: 弘安贊治河；

translations.literal: Hong'an assisted in governing the rivers;
translations.idiomatic: Hong'an was known for his work on river control;

sentences.zh: 繻善斷獄；

translations.literal: Xu was skilled in deciding cases;
translations.idiomatic: Xu was known for his skill in judging cases;

sentences.zh: 孟球能應變：使得為督撫，其績效當有大於是者。

translations.literal: Mengqiu could respond to changing circumstances: had he been made governor or governor-general, his achievements would surely have been greater than this.
translations.idiomatic: Mengqiu could meet emergencies: had he reached the rank of governor or governor-general, his achievements would surely have been greater still.

sentences.zh: 時方承平，仕得行其意，知止知足，必有說以自處矣。

translations.literal: The age was one of peace; in office they could carry out their intent, knew when to stop and when to be content, and surely had reasons by which to settle their own conduct.
translations.idiomatic: It was a time of peace; they could govern as they wished, knew when to stop and when they had enough, and no doubt had their own reasons for stepping back.
